findings.rule_quote: Waiting period for pre-existing diseases disclosed by the persons to be insured, shall be maximum up to 36 months of continuous coverage under the Health Insurance policy.

admission_date.quote: The complainant was firstly admitted in Sohana Hospital, Sector 77, Mohali from 02.10.2024 to 06.10.2024 for his left knee surgery

inception_date.quote: which was valid w.e.f. 21.04.2024 to 20.04.2025 covering himself and his wife Smt. Asha Rani for cashless treatment upto Rs.10 lakhs

policy_renewal_date.quote: The principal controversy is whether the appellants have been able to establish that the respondent/complainant was suffering from Osteoarthritis (OA) of the left knee prior to inception of the subject policy on 21.04.2024 and had knowingly suppressed the said material fact.

ported_from_date.quote: initially he had been obtaining the health insurance policies from National Insurance Company Ltd. since 25.04.2019 to 24.04.2024 (Annexures A-5 to A-9) on payment of the due premium amounts without any default.

alleged_undisclosed_condition.quote: Osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee is a chronic, degenerative and progressive condition, which develops over several years and cannot arise suddenly after inception of the policy.

findings.question_en: For how many continuous months has this policyholder been covered?
findings.action_en: Point out that the waiting period cannot exceed the cap; ask the insurer to reconsider.
